title: Relative approximation of a formal isomorphism with a varying base map
statement: Let $X\to S$ and $Y\to T$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme] locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and suppose $S$ and $T$ are of finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. Let $x\in X$, $s\in S$, $y\in Y$, and $t\in T$ satisfy $x\mapsto s$ and $y\mapsto t$. Put $A=\mathcal O_{S,s}$ and let $\sigma:\mathcal O_{T,t}\to\widehat A$ be a local ring homomorphism (it sends the maximal ideal into that of $\widehat A$). Completions here and below are maximal-ideal-adic [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Form $Y_\sigma=Y\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\widehat A$ [def-pc-fibre-product], using $\operatorname{Spec}\widehat A\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{T,t}\to T$. Suppose $y_\sigma\in Y_\sigma$ maps to $y$ and to the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}\widehat A$, and an isomorphism $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,x}\cong\widehat{\mathcal O}_{Y_\sigma,y_\sigma}$ of $\widehat A$-algebras is given. Then there exist a pointed étale morphism $(V,v)\to(S,s)$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], a morphism $\tau:V\to T$ with $\tau(v)=t$, and a scheme $U$ with point $u$, equipped with an étale morphism $(U,u)\to(X,x)$ and an étale $V$-morphism $U\to Y\times_{T,\tau}V$. The maps commute over $S$ and $V$, and $u\mapsto v$. The induced maps $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(v)$ and $\kappa(x)\to\kappa(u)$ [def-weil-residue-field] are isomorphisms. No equality of the resulting formal map with the original formal isomorphism is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0GDX, lemma-relative-map-approximation-pre, specialized to a base S of finite type over the integers (whose local rings are G-rings).

proof.text: Work on affine neighbourhoods $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $T=\operatorname{Spec}D$, and affine neighbourhoods of $x$ and $y$ mapping into them. Open immersions are etale and compositions of etale maps are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation], so a diagram for these neighbourhoods gives one for the original schemes. The bases are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. By [lem-trf-integers-excellent] and [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent], $R$ and $A=R_{\mathfrak p}=\mathcal O_{S,s}$ are excellent; the definition [def-exc-excellent-ring] gives that $A$ is a Noetherian G-ring. The affine coordinate algebras of $X/S$ and $Y/T$ are finite type by hypothesis, hence finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation].

source.place: Tag 0GDX hypotheses; affine reductions in its proof; Tags 07QU, 07QW and 00FP

proof.text: Put $B=\operatorname{Spec}\widehat A$, with closed point $b$. The ring $\widehat A$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian]. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring] its maximal ideal is $\mathfrak m_A\widehat A$ and its residue field is $\kappa(s)$; [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal] makes it complete for that ideal. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-g-ring] applies to $\widehat A$. Put $X_B=X\times_SB$, with point $x_B$ over $(x,b)$. Its closed fibre is $X_s$, since $\kappa(b)=\kappa(s)$, so $\kappa(x_B)=\kappa(x)$. The completed-local identification [lem-trf-completed-local-base-change] identifies its completed stalk with $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{X,x}$ as a $\widehat A$-algebra. The families $X_B/B$ and $Y_\sigma/B$ are locally finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change]. Apply [lem-trf-isomorphism-completion-approximation] with $N=2$ and the inverse of the transported given isomorphism. This gives a span $X_B\leftarrow(U,u)\to Y_\sigma$ over $B$, both arrows etale, with $\kappa(x_B)\cong\kappa(u)\cong\kappa(y_\sigma)$.

source.place: Tag 0GDX proof, first paragraph; Tag 0CAV; Algebra Tags 0316, 05GG, 05GI

proof.text: The localization $R\to A$ is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-regular], and $A\to\widehat A$ is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-g-ring-completion-regular]. For a prime $\mathfrak q\subset R$, the fibre of $R\to\widehat A$ is zero if $\mathfrak q\not\subset\mathfrak p$, and otherwise is the fibre of $A\to\widehat A$ at $\mathfrak qA$; hence it is Noetherian. Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-regular-composition] makes $R\to\widehat A$ regular. Both rings are Noetherian, so [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-smoothing] writes $\widehat A$ as a colimit over a small filtered category of smooth $R$-algebras. Reindex by a nonempty directed set using [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-category-directed-cofinal]. By [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition], $B=\varprojlim_i S_i$ as schemes, with $S_i$ affine and smooth over $S$.

source.place: Tag 0GDX proof, second paragraph; Tags 0AH2, 07QI, 07GC, 0032 and 01YW

proof.text: Let $s_i$ be the image of $b$ in $S_i$. The field maps $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(s_i)\to\kappa(b)=\kappa(s)$ have composite the identity. The second map is injective and its image contains all of $\kappa(s)$, so both maps are isomorphisms. These are the actual residue maps induced by $B\to S_i\to S$.

The affine target $T$ is finitely presented over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-map-limit-factorization] over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ to the map $B\to T$ defined by $\sigma$. After restricting to stages $j\geq i_0$, it factors through $\sigma_{i_0}:S_{i_0}\to T$; write $\sigma_j$ for its composite with $S_j\to S_{i_0}$. In particular $\sigma_j(s_j)=t$. Fix, from now on, $X_j=X\times_SS_j$ and $Y_j=Y\times_{T,\sigma_j}S_j$. These are affine schemes of finite presentation over $S_j$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition]. Their actual pullbacks to $B$ are $X_B$ and $Y_\sigma$. Shrink $U$ to an affine neighbourhood of $u$. Its map to the affine $X_B$ is etale, hence locally of finite presentation [def-weil-etale-morphism]; on affines the coordinate map is finitely presented, and composition in [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition] gives that $U/B$ is of finite presentation. Restricting an etale map to an open remains etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation].

source.place: Tag 0GDX proof, second and third paragraphs; Tag 01ZC and algebraic finite-presentation permanence

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-fixed-family-etale-span-descent] to the affine limit $B=\varprojlim S_j$, the point $b$, the fixed models $P_0=X_{i_0}$ and $Q_0=Y_{i_0}$, and the span from step 2. Step 4 supplies every required base residue-field isomorphism, and step 5 supplies finite presentation and the actual pullback identifications. It gives a stage $j$, a scheme $U_j$, etale arrows $U_j\to X_j$ and $U_j\to Y_j$, and an isomorphism $U_j\times_{S_j}B\cong U$ intertwining both arrows. Define $u_j$ as the image of $u$, $x_j$ as the image of $x_B$, and $y_j$ as the image of $y_\sigma$. The lemma gives $\kappa(u_j)\cong\kappa(u)$, $\kappa(x_j)\cong\kappa(x_B)$, $\kappa(y_j)\cong\kappa(y_\sigma)$, and residue-field isomorphisms for both stage arrows. In particular $\kappa(u_j)=\kappa(x)$. Only $U$ and its arrows have been descended; the two target models remain the specified fibre products.

source.place: Tag 0GDX proof, third paragraph; fixed-family pointed refinement of Tags 01ZM and 07RP

proof.text: Since $S_j\to S$ is smooth and $\kappa(s_j)=\kappa(s)$, [lem-trf-finite-residue-point-closed-in-fibre] makes $s_j$ closed in its fibre. The identity residue extension is finite separable, so [lem-trf-smooth-point-etale-immersion] gives an immersion $V\to S_j$ through $s_j$, etale over $S$, with singleton underlying fibre over $s$. By the definition of immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], shrink $S_j$ around $s_j$ so that this immersion is closed, and restrict $U_j,X_j,Y_j$ to that open. Restriction preserves the two etale arrows by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. Write $v\in V$ for the point mapping to $s_j$, so $\kappa(v)=\kappa(s_j)=\kappa(s)$. Set $\tau=\sigma_j|_V$; then $\tau(v)=t$.

source.place: Tag 0GDX proof, final paragraph; Tags 01TE and 057G

proof.text:
Put $W=U_j\times_{S_j}V$. The universal property of fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product] gives, compatibly with every projection,
\[
W\cong U_j\times_{X_j}(X\times_SV),\qquad
W\cong U_j\times_{Y_j}(Y\times_TV).
\]
Indeed a test-scheme map into either right-hand side is exactly a pair of maps to $U_j,V$ agreeing in $S_j$, because $X_j=X\times_SS_j$ and $Y_j=Y\times_TS_j$. Thus $W\to X\times_SV$ and $W\to Y\times_TV$ are actual base changes of the two etale stage arrows. They are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits]. The projection $X\times_SV\to X$ is a base change of $V\to S$, hence etale by the same node, and $W\to X$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. All triangles commute by the displayed universal properties.

source.place: Tag 0GDX proof, final paragraph: Cartesian identifications and conclusion

proof.text: On an affine neighbourhood of $s_j$, write $V=\operatorname{Spec}(C/J)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}C\subseteq S_j$. By the closed-immersion definition [def-weil-closed-immersion], $J$ vanishes in $\kappa(s_j)$, hence in $\kappa(u_j)$. The fibre of $W=U_j\times_{S_j}V$ over $u_j$ is therefore $\operatorname{Spec}(\kappa(u_j)\otimes_C C/J)=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u_j)$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. It has a unique point $w$, with $\kappa(w)=\kappa(u_j)=\kappa(x)$. Also $w\mapsto v$ and $\kappa(v)=\kappa(s)$. Taking $(U,u)=(W,w)$ now gives every required clause.
